Students may include some of the following points, but all other relevant points must be credited:
• Christianity — many Christians prioritise reformation, following Jesus's teaching about forgiveness and second chances. The Parable of the Lost Son (Luke 15:11-32) shows that God welcomes back those who have done wrong, suggesting that the purpose of punishment should be to help criminals change.
• Islam — the Qur'an records the principle of proportional retribution as a ruling first given to the Children of Israel: 'We ordained for them: a life for a life, an eye for an eye' (5:45). The same verse praises anyone who forgoes it as charity, so while retribution is permitted, forgiveness and reformation are preferred. Islamic law calls this principle qisas.
